judgments.reasoning_cat1: The offer terms (start date, contingency on screenings, void-if-no-commencement) are concrete, though the Agreement's stated effective date (signature) sits oddly against the condition that employment begin on or before April 16, 2012.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶7 (employment at will) and ¶20 (entire agreement); nothing directly contradicts the offer paragraph, and the 'Effective Date' definition is used consistently in the signature block.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such instructional materials and other assistance as Wells Fargo Advisors in its sole discretion deems reasonable and necessary' and 'expected to complete satisfactorily' are soft, standardless terms, but they impose little operative obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10(a), which prices 'Training Costs' for participation in the very Program described here without tying those costs to anything the company actually provided; the fit is loose but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'At least initially, you will be eligible for overtime pay' is genuinely indeterminate as to duration, and compensation is delegated to a Plan 'as that Plan may be modified from time to time' or 'as may be otherwise determined ... in its sole discretion'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶4, which ends overtime eligibility on the title change, and ¶8, which exempts compensation plans from the no-oral-modification rule; these harmonise the 'at least initially' language rather than conflicting with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The trigger (licenses plus graduation) and the consequence (monthly compensation and draw, no overtime) are stated definitely, with only the usual dependence on the external Compensation Plan.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶3 (initial overtime eligibility) and ¶10(b)(i), which measures the five-year period from the graduation date used here; the provisions dovetail rather than clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May lead to consequences, up to and including termination' is open-ended, and 'your test dates will extended' is a plain mechanical omission of 'be'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶7 (at-will) and ¶10, which conditions relief from Training Costs on graduation and five years' service — termination from the Program under this paragraph still leaves the employee liable, a harsh but not incoherent fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The prohibition list is enumerated (i)-(iv) after 'the following', which is closed, but the surrounding duty to obey 'all ... internal rules, regulations, policies and procedures' is boundless and the subparagraph numbering is garbled in the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶8 and ¶20 (entire agreement / no representations): this paragraph expressly preserves outside Wells Fargo HR policies and guidelines, which sits in some tension with the integration language.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The at-will language is standard, emphatic and internally consistent; the only softness is 'no other practice, written or oral policy or statement by anyone can alter' the at-will status.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10(b)(i), which forgives Training Costs only on five years' continuous employment, and ¶10(a), which triggers repayment on termination 'for any reason' including termination by the employer — a claimed inconsistency between at-will employment and a five-year repayment lock is exactly the kind of whole-instrument argument a court would face.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Describing a signed, binding instrument as serving 'only as a synopsis of the compensation and other arrangements' is a genuinely ambiguous characterisation that could be read to subordinate the document to unstated plans and policies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶20 ('This Agreement constitutes the entire understanding') and ¶6 (Agreement does not supersede HR policies): the 'synopsis' framing and the integration clause pull in different directions about what governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Compensation earned and received by Wells Fargo Advisors', 'fronted' revenue and 'deficit balances (unrelated to the offset of the draw)' are undefined and could reasonably be read more than one way, all subject to the elastic 'to the fullest extent permitted under applicable law'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶9(b) (no claim to revenue unless employed on the payout date), ¶10(d) (setoff of Training Costs) and ¶13(c) (adjustments to Net Eligible Revenue); these overlap on final-pay calculation but are broadly reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The forfeiture rule turns on being 'employed on the date such payments are received' and separately on the 'applicable payout date', two different reference points within one short paragraph, and 'utle to' is a typo for 'title to'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶9(a), which promises liability for 'compensation earned and received by Wells Fargo Advisors, and/or salary earned but not yet paid' before termination; that undertaking is hard to square with the total forfeiture stated here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The two dollar figures are illegible/omitted in the executed text ('QeeEeer', 'GeEeed'), so the amount of the central obligation cannot be read off the provision, and 'terminated for any reason at any time' is absolute on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10(b)(ii)(A), which erases the obligation unless the employee joins a Competitive Organization within a year, and ¶7's at-will terms; the flat repayment duty and the competition-contingent exception define the obligation very differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The five-year clock is defined precisely by the later of two dated events, and 'continuous employment' is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10(c), whose 1/48 amortization runs from the start of employment as a New FA rather than from graduation/registration, so the two schedules can expire at materially different times; ¶10(b)(ii)(C) also cross-references this period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Competitive Organization or Entity' is defined by a specific list closed with 'any other person, firm, corporation, or entity that competes with Wells Fargo Advisors' and prefaced by 'including, but not be limited to' — a classic open catch-all against enumerated specifics, plus a grammatical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10(a) (unconditional repayment), ¶10(c) (amortization) and ¶12 (one-year non-solicitation): this exception converts the repayment duty into a de facto non-compete, and its one-year window does not match the five-year period of ¶10(b)(i).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The parenthetical expressly excludes relocation from 'closed', and the causal requirement ('as a consequence') is stated plainly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10(a) and ¶10(c); this exception simply removes the repayment duty in a defined case and creates no visible clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Permanent disability' is undefined and the cross-reference is misprinted as 'Paragraph 10(b)(1)' rather than 10(b)(i), though the referent is obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10(b)(i): the exception is measured by that five-year period while ¶10(c) amortizes from the start of New FA employment, so the death/disability window may not align with the amortization schedule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amortization mechanics are stated in numbers but the start point ('beginning with the first month of the second year after your have begun employment') is ungrammatical and it is not obvious whether the 48 monthly reductions run to a four- or five-year end point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶10(b)(i), which forgives costs after five years measured from graduation/registration, not from the start of employment; the two provisions can yield different residual balances at the same date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and hedged entirely by 'to the maximum extent permitted under applicable law', which leaves little for a court to construe in the words themselves.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Checked against ¶9(a) (recovery and offset at termination) and ¶13(c) (adjustments to Net Eligible Revenue); the setoff rights overlap but do not contradict.
